core_obligations: Induction set-up (proof lines 19768-19770): prove the bound by induction on dim(X), reducing to showing that the cohomology of an abelian torsion sheaf F on X_etale vanishes above dim(X) + cd(K).

Case dim(X) = 0 (proof lines 19773-19779): if the dimension is zero the structure morphism X -> Spec(K) is finite, so its higher direct images vanish and the Leray spectral sequence bounds the cohomology of F by that of K.

Reduction for positive dimension (proof lines 19785-19795): for d = dim(X) > 1, Noether normalization provides a finite morphism from a suitable open piece of X to an affine space of dimension d, which by the induction hypothesis and the base case reduces the bound to the smooth case.

Interlude I (proof lines 19798-19828): for an open immersion j : X -> Y of smooth d-dimensional varieties over K whose complement is the support of an effective Cartier divisor D, the author analyses the sheaves involved, which is the local computation feeding the final step.

Interlude II (proof lines 19831-19850): for a smooth variety Z of dimension d-1 the author studies the subsets E_a of points of transcendence degree at most a and their behaviour, which controls the fibres of the projection used in the final diagram.

Final assembly (proof lines 19853-19913): the commutative diagram with the open immersion j : A^d_K -> P^1_K x_K A^{d-1}_K and the projection g is used to combine Interludes I and II with the induction hypothesis, yielding the bound.
proof_roadmap: Induct on the dimension of the affine scheme of finite type over K.
Dimension zero: the structure morphism is finite, so higher direct images vanish and Leray gives the bound.
Positive dimension: use Noether normalization to reduce to a smooth situation of the same dimension.
Analyse the open immersion into a product with the projective line (Interlude I) and the fibres of the projection (Interlude II).
Assemble the diagram to obtain the general bound from the induction hypothesis and the curve case.
difficulty_reason: The proposition bounds the cohomological dimension of an affine scheme of finite type over a field: cd(X) at most dim(X) + cd(K) (statement lines 19762-19766). The proof is an induction on the dimension whose hard part is the positive-dimensional case, and it contains two auxiliary arguments the author isolates as Interlude I and Interlude II: the first analyses an open immersion j : X -> Y of smooth d-dimensional varieties with complement the support of an effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 19798-19828), the second studies the loci of points of bounded transcendence degree in a smooth variety of dimension d-1 (proof lines 19831-19850). These feed the final commutative diagram involving the open immersion A^d_K -> P^1_K x_K A^{d-1}_K and the projection to A^{d-1}_K, which combines with the induction hypothesis and the curve case to give the bound (proof lines 19853-19913). The non-formal content is the reduction of the general case to the smooth situation together with the two interludes. The claim is H2: a long argument, entirely written out, with Noether normalization and the curve bound as its only inputs.
